correctness.rationale: For any n>=d>=1 unit-norm equal-prior pure tight frame, rho_B=I_d/d and rho_XB has exactly n eigenvalues 1/n. For any POVM, P_guess<=d/n since projectors <=I; the tight-frame POVM E_x=(d/n)|psi_x><psi_x| sums to I and attains d/n. The uniform-rank subentropy identity Q(I_r/r plus zeros)=log r-H_r+1 follows analytically from the normalized-simplex representation: sum of first r Dirichlet(1,...,1) coordinates S has Beta(r,N-r), with E[S]=r/N and E[S log S]=(r/N)(H_r-H_N). Hence Q(X|B)=log(n/d)-(H_n-H_d), gap from H_min exactly H_n-H_d, equality iff n=d (square frame orthonormal); all logs natural and ambient zeros handled. Independent beta-integral and harmonic checks corroborate concrete dimensions; analytic derivation controls all frames and all n.

originality.rationale: Datta-Dorlas-Jozsa-Benatti introduce conditional subentropy, prove the two-label pure-state case and explicitly conjecture Q(X|B)<=H_min. Tight-frame optimal discrimination p_guess=d/n was already proved in quantum measurement/frame work including Eldar-Forney and Farokhi-Xiao; it is credited, not new. Their statements do not compute the harmonic-number conditional subentropy gap for every tight frame. This resolves a meaningful all-dimensional sector of the conjecture, conditional on the exact uniform-rank simplex formula, with no equiangularity requirement.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-dimensional conditional subentropy computation may exist in unindexed projective-one-design or ensemble coding literature.
Farokhi-Xiao manuscript full text was not obtained; its indexed discrimination theorem is credited as prior, not denied as whole-document noncoverage.
